references.text: Here it is told about Gershom's birth and the meaning of his name: 'I have been a stranger in a foreign land'
The continuation that mentions the second son, Eliezer, and explains the meaning of his name
Moses took his wife and sons with him when he returned to Egypt
Abraham describes himself as a stranger and sojourner, the same theme found in Gershom's name
God tells Abraham that his descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own
The book of Hebrews refers to the patriarchs who confessed that they were strangers and foreigners on earth
Peter exhorts believers as strangers and foreigners, addressing the same theme of being strangers in the world
This verse confirms that Gershom was one of Moses' two sons, completing the information about the family composition found in the source verse.
This verse summarizes the period of Moses' exile in Midian and the birth of his sons, providing the historical context for the naming mentioned in the source verse.
